notes.text: ROOT CAUSE FOUND — bigger than the size violation itself. check.sh's scripts=(check.sh plugins/*/bin/*.sh plugins/*/lib/*.sh) globs on .sh, and bin/tq has NO extension. tq is the ONLY extensionless file in bin/, so THE task queue was invisible to ShellCheck (line 71), portability-lint (line 80) AND the 300-line size guard (line 100) — all three. That is why the gate stayed green at 382 lines, and why the growth from 355 went unremarked. Verified tq is CLEAN under both shellcheck and portability-lint, so wiring it in cost nothing there; the size guard is now a NAMED, PRINTED exemption pointing at this task, with a staleness check that goes RED once tq drops back under 300 so the exemption cannot outlive the problem.

MEASURED decomposition (not estimated): tq is 382, needs ≤300, so 82+ lines must go. Blocks: usage() 21 lines (cold path, help text, zero risk) · orphans verb ~38 incl. its comment (diagnostic, NOT queue mechanics, already has its own tests) · report() 60 (presentation, but HOT — called by done/import/session-start) · stopfields() 20 (MUST stay: tq owns 'first startable task', and the recorded drift bug was the Stop hook re-deriving it). usage+orphans = 59, which is 23 SHORT of the cap — so the cohesion-correct split does not reach 300 without touching report(), and that is the real decision.
